Name: CRR - Time Based Rule Triggers in E1 (Analysis, Build)
Description: As a Compliance Analyst/Manager, I want to implement time-based rule triggers so that specific risk elements and their associated rules can be evaluated on a monthly basis instead of daily, optimizing system performance and aligning with business relevance. Rules such as length of customer relationship do not require daily re-evaluation since their values change gradually over time. A configuration flag set at the risk element level through the CRR modal will designate whether all rules within the element should be considered time-based. The system will fetch this configuration at runtime and trigger rescoring only if the last scoring event occurred more than 30 days ago.  Business BenefitsReduces unnecessary compute load by avoiding daily re-evaluation of stable metricsImproves system scalability and performance during CRR batch runsEnables business-driven configurability for batch timing of risk scoringEnsures technical design supports future extensibility without redevelopmentUser ScenariosDuring a CRR batch run, the system checks if a risk element is time-based and evaluates only if 30 days have passed since last scoringSystem skips time-based rules that are not yet due, ensuring scoring logic is optimized for batch performanceA Compliance Analyst/Manager requests a change to the evaluation frequency from 30 to 45 days, and engineering updates the configuration without rewriting the feature  Non-Functional RequirementsScoring execution logic must retrieve time-based flags dynamicallyRescoring logic must track last evaluation timestamps accuratelyParameter for time-based evaluation frequency must be externalized and easily changeableAvailability target of 99.9 percent for batch execution processLogging and audit trail must capture rule execution decision logic clearly DependenciesPredecessor:  Discovery and Analysis complete in F717256CRR framework modal for rule element flaggingBatch scoring engine for time-based logic injectionScheduling service to support monthly evaluation cycleCRR configuration repository for storing and retrieving evaluation intervals Out of ScopeUI redesign for element-level time-based configurationSupport for mixed time-based and daily rules within a single risk elementReal-time rule re-evaluation outside of batch process RisksIncorrect flagging of time-based elements may lead to delayed risk updatesPoor modularization may result in future change requests requiring reworkLack of alignment between UI configuration and backend enforcement may cause inconsistency
Acceptance Criteria: Scope for a new customer/account is added, then the time based rules won't have a score until the time based rules are triggered.  Acceptance CriteriaGiven a risk elementWhen all rules within it are flagged as time-basedThen the system must evaluate those rules only once every 30 days Given a risk elementWhen it is not flagged as time-basedThen the system must continue evaluating its rules on a daily basis Given a CRR batch runWhen a time-based rule is eligible for executionThen the system must execute and log the updated score Given a configuration change from 30 days to another valueWhen implementedThen the system must apply the new threshold without code refactoring

Name: CRR - Rule Change Based Rule Triggers in E1 (Analysis, Build)
Description: As a Compliance Analyst / Manager, I want the CRR platform to support triggering rescoring whenever a rule is changed within the CRR framework so that risk scoring remains aligned with the most current compliance logic and customer risk ratings reflect updated rule definitions. When a user modifies a rule through the CRR risk framework interface, a trigger must be generated by the UI and sent to the risk scoring system. The scoring system must consume this event, identify the rule delta, and then evaluate whether rescoring is necessary. If required, rescoring must be performed using the updated rule set, and the newly calculated customer risk ratings must be returned. This feature is intended to drive discovery and analysis work, identifying all scenarios and edge cases in which rescoring must be triggered based on rule-level changes. Business BenefitsEnsures customer risk scores are dynamically updated in response to regulatory or business rule changesReduces manual coordination between compliance and engineering by automating scoring triggersStrengthens accuracy of risk decisions by capturing scoring changes in near real-timeEstablishes baseline for robust event-driven architecture to support CRR evolution User ScenariosA Compliance Analyst modifies a data point mapping within an existing rule; the system sends a trigger to the scoring engine to initiate rescoringA Compliance Analyst / Manager updates a rule’s multiplier value; the system identifies the change and initiates rescoring for affected customersThe tech team performs an analysis of rule modifications including multiplier adjustments, data point reclassification, rule activation/deactivation, or changes to evaluation conditionsSystem processes a rule update event, computes deltas, and performs rescoring only for customers impacted by the specific changeDiscovery identifies edge cases such as shared rules across risk elements, conflicting rule reuse, or rules embedded in multiple market-specific contexts  Non-Functional RequirementsDelta detection logic must operate with low latency and high reliabilityRule change event schema must be standardized and version-controlledAudit trail must capture who made the rule change, what was changed, and the resulting scoring impactDiscovery outputs must be presented in a format usable for future automation and test coverageAvailability target of 99.9 percent for scoring service and event listeners DependenciesCRR framework UI for rule editing and submissionEvent sourcing system to send and receive rule change triggersScoring engine capable of evaluating rule-level deltasCustomer data repository for scoring contextMonitoring and alerting tools for trigger processing Out of ScopeScoring for data changes not related to rule logicSandbox-based scoring simulationsFull UI redesign for rule submission flow RisksUnmapped rule scenarios may result in incomplete rescoring coverageMisidentified deltas could cause over- or under-scoringEvent delivery failures may lead to stale customer ratingsEdge cases involving rule inheritance or composite logic may introduce complexity
Acceptance Criteria: Acceptance CriteriaGiven a rule change is made through the CRR frameworkWhen the update is submittedThen the UI must send a trigger event to the scoring engine with change metadata Given the scoring engine receives the triggerWhen the rule change is processedThen it must analyze and detect the delta introduced by the rule update Given customer data relevant to the changed ruleWhen the delta indicates a scoring impactThen the engine must perform rescoring for those affected customers Given rule changes across different types and configurationsWhen analyzing the full CRR rule catalogThen the team must document all triggering scenarios and edge cases
